nodes.label: CI CD Pipeline
nodes.summary: The trigger and orchestrator of the whole framework. On every push, merge request or schedule it decides which jobs run, in which stage, on which runner, and where the evidence is published. Three equivalent pipelines exist (GitLab CI, Jenkins, GitHub Actions) so the framework is not tied to one CI vendor.
features: GitLab stages: `config → build → test → report → pages`
`generate-pipeline-config` job reads `pipeline-config.properties` to decide which sites are enabled (fail closed for sites)
Quality jobs: `checkstyle`, `unit-tests`, `security-scan` (OWASP), `secret-scan` (gitleaks), `coverage-gate`
Test jobs: `test` (web, parallel), `mobile-test` (Appium), `api-tests`, `accessibility-visual-test`, `perf-tests`, `perf-smoke`
`test-impact-analysis` job selects only the tests affected by the change
`report` job merges Allure/Extent output; `pages` publishes it; `notify` posts to chat
Same flow mirrored in `Jenkinsfile` and GitHub Actions (`github-ci.yml`, `gh-pages-retention.yml`)
Python helper scripts compute flaky trend, coverage summary, dashboard history, PR comments
nodes.short: Starts every test run automatically when code changes.
bullets: Runs on GitLab, Jenkins or GitHub
Checks code quality and security first
Runs web, mobile, API and speed tests
Publishes the report and notifies chat

nodes.label: Build Tool
nodes.summary: The single entry point that compiles the framework and launches tests. Every CI job and every developer command is just `mvn …` with different properties and profiles, so local runs and CI runs behave identically.
features: Maven 3.9+ with the Maven Wrapper (`mvnw`) — no global install needed
`maven-surefire-plugin` reads `-DsuiteXmlFile=testng-suites/<suite>.xml` and forks a JVM (`-Xmx2048m`)
Properties forwarded to the forked JVM: `-Dsite`, `-Dbrowser`, `-Dgrid.enabled`, `-Dcoverage.map.enabled`, `-Dreportportal.enable`
Opt-in profiles: `perf`, `security`, `mutation`, `unit-tests`, `tia`, `bug-crawler`, `mobile-bug-crawler`, `prune-artifacts`, `coverage-map`, `reportportal`
Quality plugins: Checkstyle gate, JaCoCo (prepare-agent / report / merge / check), OWASP dependency-check, JMeter
`allure-maven` generates the Allure report from `target/allure-results`
Dependency management for Selenium 4.21, TestNG 7.9, Rest-Assured, Appium, DataFaker, AShot, axe-core
nodes.short: Compiles the code and launches the tests with one command.
bullets: Same on a laptop and in CI

nodes.label: Grid Infrastructure
nodes.summary: The execution fabric. Instead of launching browsers on the CI host, tests open `RemoteWebDriver` sessions against a Dockerized Selenium Grid, so browsers are isolated, parallel and reproducible. The same compose files run on a laptop or a CI server.
features: Selenium Hub 4.21.0 with event bus on ports 4442 / 4443
Browser nodes: `node-chrome`, `node-firefox`, `node-edge` (4.21.0), each `SE_NODE_MAX_SESSIONS=3`, `shm_size: 3gb`
Live viewing through noVNC on each node
`tests` container runs the suite inside the same Docker network
Autoscale override (`docker-compose.autoscale.yml`) + `grid-autoscaler.py` adds/removes nodes with queue depth
Automation Console dashboard (`docker-compose.dashboard.yml`, `Dockerfile.dashboard`)
Switched on with `-Dgrid.enabled=true`; hub address from `grid.url` (default `http://localhost:4444/wd/hub`)
Thread-count 3 in suite XML is deliberately aligned with `SE_NODE_MAX_SESSIONS=3`
nodes.short: A farm of ready-made browsers running in Docker.
bullets: Chrome, Firefox and Edge on demand
Many tests at the same time
Watch tests live in the browser

nodes.label: Test Runner
nodes.summary: Decides what runs and how in parallel. TestNG suite XML files select groups and classes; test-config.properties can switch individual tests off without touching code; retry and selection logic are plugged in through listeners.
features: TestNG 7.9.0 suites in `testng-suites/` (22 XMLs): smoke, regression, api, accessibility, perf, mobile, safari …
`parallel="classes" thread-count="3"` — one thread, one driver per class; methods stay sequential
Group-driven selection: `smoke`, `regression`, `api`, `perf`, `accessibility`, `visual`, `keyword-driven`, `data-driven`, `synthetic-data`
`RetryListener` (IAnnotationTransformer) attaches `RetryAnalyzer` to every `@Test` — registered in suite XML
`TestSelectionListener` applies `test-config.properties` (fail open: never silently drops a test)
ServiceLoader auto-registration: coverage-map listeners and ReportPortal agent
Safari suites are separate (macOS only, no headless, one session per machine)
nodes.short: Chooses which tests run and runs them in parallel.
bullets: Pick tests by label: smoke, regression…
Three tests run side by side

nodes.label: Base Test Class
nodes.summary: The lifecycle parent of every test. It creates a driver per thread before each method, hands it to page objects, cleans up afterwards, and guarantees teardown even when a test fails. Specialised bases reuse the same idea for keyword, API and mobile tests.
features: `protected static final ThreadLocal<WebDriver> driver` — safe parallel execution
`@BeforeMethod(alwaysRun = true)` → `DriverFactory.createDriver()` → `driver.set(...)`
`@AfterMethod` / `@AfterClass(alwaysRun = true)` → `DriverFactory.quitDriver(...)` and orphan-process cleanup
`@Listeners({TestListener.class})` wires reporting/evidence callbacks
MDC tagging so every log line carries the test name
Method-scoped and class-scoped cleanup (`CleanupRegistry`) for API-seeded data
Variants: `KeywordTestBase` (CSV-driven), `BaseApiTest` (Rest-Assured), `MobileBaseTest` (Appium), `DemoQaBaseTest` (site-level)
nodes.short: Gives every test its own fresh browser and cleans up after.
bullets: Logs tagged with the test name

nodes.label: Data Driven Engine
nodes.summary: Separates test logic from test data. One `DataRow` shape is produced from five file formats plus a synthetic generator, and a keyword engine lets whole scenarios be written as CSV rows with no Java at all.
features: `DataProviderFactory.fromFile / fromSheet / fromFileWithTags / fromFileUnfiltered`
Readers for CSV, Excel (`.xlsx`), JSON, YAML and ZIP behind one `DataFileReader` interface and `DataFileReaderRegistry`
Unified `DataRow` model — same shape from every format
Synthetic data: `SyntheticDataGenerator` / `syntheticRegistrations()` and edge-case sets (DataFaker)
Keyword-driven: `KeywordReader` → `KeywordStep` → `KeywordEngine` (`NAVIGATE`, `TYPE`, `CLICK`, `VERIFY_*` …)
`ObjectRepository` maps logical names to locators; `PlaceholderResolver` injects values
Errors surface as `DataFileException` / `KeywordExecutionException`
stack: Apache POI · opencsv · Jackson · SnakeYAML readers
nodes.short: Runs the same test with many sets of data.
bullets: Reads CSV, Excel, JSON, YAML, ZIP
Keeps data apart from test logic

nodes.label: Page Objects
nodes.summary: The Page Object Model layer: one class per page, exposing business actions (`login()`, `fillForm()`) while hiding locators and waits. Adding a new site means adding page classes — nothing else in the framework changes.
features: 34 page classes — DemoQA (Elements, Forms, Widgets, Interactions, Book Store), SauceDemo `LoginPage`, Android `SettingsHomePage`
Each page extends `BasePage` (or `BaseMobilePage`) and receives the driver in its constructor
Reusable components: `ReactDatePickerComponent`, `BootstrapModalComponent`
`TemplatePage` + `Scripts/new-site.sh` / `new-api-site.sh` scaffold a new site
Locators for keyword tests live in `objectrepository/<site>.properties`
Per-site config: `config/<site>.properties` selected by `-Dsite=<name>`
nodes.tagline: One class per page, no locators in tests
nodes.short: One class per web page, so tests read like plain steps.
bullets: New site = new page classes only

nodes.label: Base Page Wrapper
nodes.summary: The wrapper around raw Selenium. Every page object inherits explicit waits, safe clicks, healing and human-like pacing from this one class — the "one chokepoint per concern" principle — so tests never call `driver.findElement` directly.
features: `abstract class BasePage` with `driver`, `WebDriverWait`, `JavascriptExecutor`
Helpers: `waitVisible`, `waitClickable`, `getText`, `isDisplayed`, `scrollAndJsClick`, `navigateTo`
`SelfHealingEngine` — DOM-similarity recovery when a locator breaks (opt-in visual and AI fallbacks)
`SmartLocator` — explicit hand-picked fallback locators
`HumanActions` — human-like typing/click pacing
`handleCaptchaIfPresent()` → `CaptchaSolver` (auto-solve inside keyword tests)
`dumpPageForDebugging()` page-source dump on locator failure
`BaseMobilePage` provides the same contract for Appium
nodes.short: Safe building blocks: wait, click, type — and self-repair.
bullets: Finds elements again if the page changes
Types and clicks like a human

nodes.label: Driver Manager
nodes.summary: The single place where browsers are born and die. It reads configuration, builds options for the requested browser, decides between a local driver and a Grid `RemoteWebDriver`, and guarantees cleanup — including killing orphaned driver processes.
features: Browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, Safari (macOS only) — headless where supported
`DriverFactory.createDriver()` chooses local vs `RemoteWebDriver` via `grid.enabled` / `grid.url`
Per-thread state: `ThreadLocal<DriverService>`, per-thread port slot, `ThreadLocal<Properties>` in `ConfigReader`
Three-layer config: `global.properties` → `<site>.properties` → `-Dkey=value`
`SiteRegistry` resolves the active site and base URL
`quitDriver()` and `forceKillOrphanedDriverProcess()` prevent leaked chromedriver/browser processes
Download directory management for upload/download tests
`AppiumDriverFactory` builds `AndroidDriver` / `IOSDriver` for the mobile module
Typed failures: `DriverInitializationException`, `ConfigException`
nodes.short: Creates the browser and decides where it runs.
bullets: Local browser or Grid with one switch

nodes.label: Test Listeners
nodes.summary: The nervous system of the run. TestNG calls these listeners at every test event, and they turn raw pass/fail results into evidence, retries, report entries and coverage data — without any test class having to ask for it.
features: `TestListener` implements `ITestListener` + `IInvokedMethodListener`: `onStart`, `onTestStart`, `onTestSuccess`, `onTestFailure`, `onTestSkipped`, `onTestFailedWithTimeout`, `onFinish`
On failure: triggers screenshot, page dump, video decision and optional AI failure analysis
`RetryListener` + `RetryAnalyzer` re-run flaky tests; skips retry when the failure is not retryable
`TestSelectionListener` disables tests switched off in `test-config.properties`
`JacocoPerTestCoverageListener` + `AlterSuiteForCoverageMapListener` build the per-test coverage map for TIA
Registered via `@Listeners` (BaseTest), suite XML (`RetryListener`) and ServiceLoader (the rest)
Never lets diagnostics break the test — helpers swallow their own exceptions
nodes.short: Watches every test and reacts when something happens.
bullets: Reacts to pass, fail and skip
Takes proof when a test fails

nodes.label: Media Capture
nodes.summary: Produces the visual proof for every result: screenshots, video, page-source dumps and visual diffs. Capture is centralised so every report format receives the same artifacts, and sensitive values are masked before anything is written.
features: `ScreenshotUtil.captureScreenshot / captureScreenshotAsBase64 / captureScreenshotAsBytes`
`VideoRecorder.start / stop / discard` — opt-in (`video.enabled`), one recorder per test attempt, no-op in headless runs by design
`FailureDiagnostics` collects page source and browser console logs on failure (best-effort, never fails the test)
`DebugDumpUtils` page-source dumps for locator failures
`VisualRegressionUtils` — AShot pixel diff against `visual-baselines/`
`AccessibilityUtils` — axe-core WCAG scans attached as evidence
`SensitiveData` masks passwords/tokens in logs and artifacts
`ArtifactRetentionCleaner` prunes old artifacts (retention policy)
nodes.short: Collects the proof: screenshots, video and page copies.

nodes.label: Reporting Engine
nodes.summary: Turns raw events and evidence into reports people actually read. Two reports are always produced (Allure interactive, Extent self-contained), with optional live streaming to ReportPortal and extra summaries for coverage, self-healing and impact analysis.
features: `ExtentManager` — thread-safe singleton (`getInstance`, `setActiveSuiteName`, `reset`), HTML at `target/extent-reports/<site>-report.html`
Allure results + `AllureEnvironmentWriter` (environment panel) + history trend via `allure-maven`
ReportPortal live stream through `ReportPortalTestNGListener`, switched by `-Dreportportal.enable=true`
JaCoCo HTML coverage at `target/site/jacoco/index.html`
Segmented reports per site/suite and a generated landing page
Self-healing report (`HealingEvent`, `SelfHealingReportWriter`) and TIA / crawler reports
Published by the `report` and `pages` CI jobs; chat notification summarises results
nodes.short: Turns results into reports anyone can open.

flows.label: CI job runs mvn
flows.text: A push, merge request or schedule starts the pipeline; each job calls `mvn` (or `./mvnw`) with properties such as `-Dsite`, `-Dbrowser`, `-DsuiteXmlFile`.
flows.plain: A code change starts the pipeline.

flows.label: surefire + suiteXmlFile
flows.text: Surefire forks a JVM and hands the chosen `testng-suites/*.xml` to TestNG, forwarding the `-D` properties.
flows.plain: Maven launches the chosen test suite.

flows.label: run test classes (parallel)
flows.text: TestNG runs the selected groups with `parallel="classes"`, `thread-count=3`; data rows come from the Data Driven Engine.
flows.plain: Tests start, three at a time.

flows.label: data rows
flows.text: TestNG calls the `@DataProvider` backed by the Data Driven Engine; every row (CSV, Excel, JSON, YAML, ZIP or synthetic) becomes one test invocation of the Base Test Class.
flows.plain: Each data row becomes one test.

flows.label: new Page(driver)
flows.text: The test method builds its Page Objects with the per-thread driver created in `setUp()`.
flows.plain: The test gets its pages ready to use.

flows.label: createDriver()
flows.text: `@BeforeMethod` calls `DriverFactory.createDriver()` and stores the driver in a `ThreadLocal`; the test then builds its Page Objects with that driver.

flows.label: extends
flows.text: Page classes extend `BasePage`, inheriting waits, healing, human pacing and CAPTCHA handling.
flows.plain: Pages reuse safe click and wait helpers.

flows.label: uses WebDriver
flows.text: Every click/type goes through the wrapper to the one `WebDriver` owned by the Driver Manager.
flows.plain: Every action goes through one browser.

flows.label: RemoteWebDriver session
flows.text: With `grid.enabled=true` the driver is a `RemoteWebDriver` against the Dockerized Selenium Hub; otherwise a local browser.
flows.plain: The browser runs in Docker, or locally.

flows.label: ITestListener events
flows.text: TestNG fires start / success / failure / skip / finish events; listeners are registered by annotation, suite XML and ServiceLoader.

flows.label: on failure / finish
flows.text: On failure (and optionally always) listeners ask Media Capture for screenshots, page source, console logs and video.
flows.plain: On failure, grab screenshots and logs.

flows.label: attach evidence
flows.text: Evidence is embedded in Extent, attached to Allure and optionally streamed to ReportPortal.
flows.plain: Proof is attached to the report.

flows.label: publish → next run
flows.text: The `report` and `pages` jobs publish the reports and history; chat gets a summary and the next run starts from the new baseline.
flows.plain: The report is published; the next run starts.

overview.headline: A robot tester for websites, mobile apps and APIs
overview.text: Write a test once. The framework opens a real browser, clicks like a user, checks the result, takes proof and publishes a report — automatically, on every code change.

Screenshots, logs and video as proof.
Dashboards with history, shared by link.

UI, API, mobile, visual, accessibility, speed.
GitLab, Jenkins and GitHub Actions included.
